reason: The text contains numerous regular human characters with extensive dialogue, emotional expressions, and opinions. Major characters include Mordecai (מָרְדֳּכַי), who mourns (וַיִּקְרַע מָרְדֳּכַי אֶת־ בְּגָדָיו) and expresses concern; Esther (אֶסְתֵּר), who speaks multiple times and demonstrates emotional responses; King Ahasuerus, who exhibits anger (וַיִּקְצֹף הַמֶּלֶךְ מְאֹד) and makes decisions; and Haman (הָמָן), whose emotions (חֵמָה - rage) and opinions are extensively documented. Throughout the narrative, characters engage in dialogue, express emotions like joy (שָׂמֵחַ), sorrow (אֵבֶל), and fear (פַּחַד), and demonstrate personal agency through their choices and opinions. These are not merely functional characters but complex individuals with documented emotional lives and perspectives.
